Dragon-temple — colossal scaled columns frame entrance, carved wing-motifs span architrave, half-collapsed roof reveals interior altar with dragon-skull centerpiece, ancient stone worn smooth by centuries.
Cliff-cut roost — massive cave mouth carved with dragon-face relief, jutting stone platform extends over valley, scored with talon-marks, natural rock columns frame opening darkly.
Mountain-cut tomb — enormous stone doors carved as folded dragon wings, runic glyphs glow faintly along frame, cliff face shaped into snarling dragon head above entrance.
Dragon-shrine — standing stones arranged in circle, each carved with different dragon aspect, central obsidian altar scarred by fire, weathered runes spiral up each monolith surface.
Cathedral-of-bones — massive wyrm ribs arch overhead as structural supports, fused vertebrae form pillars, wing-bones span ceiling like gothic vaults, ancient and sanctified by cult.

Dragon-rider outpost — fortress built into mountain face, wide landing platforms jutting from cliff, scaled battlements, massive chain-mechanisms hang unused, architecture designed for mounted flights.
Scaled-column hall — vast interior corridor lined with pillars carved as dragon necks, heads curve to support ceiling, jeweled eyes glint in shadows, floor polished obsidian.
Vault-of-hoards — stone treasury carved deep into mountain, dragon-claw buttresses support arched ceiling, runic wards etched across sealed door, abandoned treasure chamber looms ominously.

Dragon-cult-monastery — fortified stone complex on mountainside, dragon-wing flying buttresses extend from walls, hooded figures carved in relief worship dragon-deity central statue, crumbling but intact.
Dragon-tooth crenellations — castle wall crowned with massive carved fangs pointing skyward, each battlement shaped as dragon jaw, ancient fortress dominates ridge, silhouetted against stormy sky.
Colonnade-of-claws — processional way lined with pillars carved as dragon legs, stone talons grip earth, each column unique dragon species, path leads to distant temple ruins.

Dragon-fortified-keep — tower fortress with dragon-skull gatehouse, scaled walls rise steeply, wing-shaped parapets extend from corners, built to withstand and house dragons simultaneously, partially ruined.
Dragon-tomb-marker-field — valley floor dotted with stone monuments carved as coiled dragons, each marking ancient wyrm burial site, moss-covered sentinels stretch toward misty mountains beyond.
Aerie — high mountain platform carved from living rock, dragon-perch stones jut upward, open to sky, wind-worn stairs spiral down cliff face, abandoned roost overlooks vast landscape.

Dragon-cathedral — towering gothic structure with dragon-eye rose windows, flying buttresses shaped as folded wings, scale-textured stone walls, massive doors carved with dragon history panels, majestic ruin.

Dragon-fire altar — circular stone platform carved with flame motifs, central brazier shaped as dragon maw, surrounding pillars topped with dragon-head capitals breathe eternal flame, mountaintop temple.

Wyrm-skeleton gatehouse — colossal dragon skull forms entrance arch, vertebrae extend as tunnel walls, ribcage supports ceiling above passage, petrified remains integrated into fortress architecture permanently.
Dragon-glyph obelisk — towering stone spire carved with spiraling runic dragon script, weathered but readable, stands alone in wasteland, monument to ancient dragon-pact, lightning-scarred peak.
Scaled-dome sanctuary — domed building with roof carved as overlapping dragon scales, metallic sheen despite stone construction, dragon-claw finial tops structure, circular temple in clearing.

Dragon-watch tower — slender fortress spire with dragon-head gargoyles at corners, observation platform designed for rider-mount pairs, claw-marked stone, defensive outpost overlooking border valleys below.
Petrified-flame colonnade — row of columns carved as frozen dragonfire, orange-red veined stone, organic flame-like curves support arched roof, processional path through ancient dragon-worship site.
Dragon-throne dais — raised platform carved from single stone block, dragon-claw armrests, scaled backrest rises high, empty seat in ruined throne room, built for dragon-lord or rider-king.
Wing-vault chapel — small shrine with ceiling carved as spread dragon wings meeting at peak, feather-scale details, dragon-eye window above altar casts colored light, hillside pilgrimage site.
Dragon-horn spires — twin towers carved spiraling upward like dragon horns, linked by bridge carved as spine, fortress crown overlooks kingdom, ancient construction defies time weathering.

Claw-carved buttresses — fortress exterior reinforced by massive stone supports carved as dragon legs grasping walls, talons dig into foundation, architectural defense and dragon-homage combined, formidable stronghold.

STANDING-STONES SHRINE — Nine monoliths arranged in a broken circle across a windswept plateau, each face etched with dragon-rune columns, the central stone twice the height of the others, crowned with a carved dragon-eye socket.

DRAGON-TOMB-MARKER FIELD — Dozens of carved stone slabs extending into deep distance across scorched moorland, each marker bearing a different wyrm-sigil, the largest stones fused partially into the earth by ancient dragonfire heat.

WYRM-SKELETON SUPPORTS — Collapsed mead-hall at midground, its ridge-beam held aloft by fused vertebral columns of a long-dead wyrm, the enormous spine arching the full length of the structure, ribs splayed outward as decorative corbels.

DRAGON-TEMPLE GATE — Freestanding ceremonial archway of dark basalt, dragon-wing reliefs spreading across its full span, the passage floor inlaid with a mosaic wyrm-scale pattern, the lintel stone cracked by some enormous upward impact.

PETRIFIED-FLAME CHANDELIER HALL — Long banquet ruin at midground, ceiling hung with calcified dragonfire bursts frozen mid-bloom, each stone flame cluster the size of a cart, casting jagged shadow patterns across the debris-strewn floor below.

DRAGON-FACE CLIFF CARVING — An entire cliff-face worked into a colossal wyrm-visage at deep distance, eye sockets deep enough to shelter a mounted rider, the lower jaw forming a natural bridge spanning the ravine below.

DRAGON-TOMB — Sealed stone mausoleum half-submerged in a frozen tarn, dragon-glyph friezes running continuously around all four exterior walls, the capstone shaped as a coiled wyrm in bas-relief, frost-cracked along every joint seam.

AERIE-TOWER — Hollow cylindrical keep open at the crown, interior walls studded with iron perch-rings at multiple heights, enormous claw-scored gouges spiraling down the inner stone surface, the base ringed with scattered scale-shaped stone debris.

DRAGON-CULT MONASTERY SCRIPTORIUM — Low-vaulted stone chamber visible through a collapsed outer wall, shelving niches carved with wyrm-scale borders, a lectern carved in full dragon-torso relief standing upright amid scattered stone fragments.

SCALED-COLUMN BRIDGE — Ancient span crossing a deep gorge at midground, every parapet pillar carved in wyrm-scale relief, the central arch keystone shaped as a roaring dragon-head, two outer parapet sections eroded and crumbled away.

DRAGON-TOOTH CRENELLATED WALL — Long defensive curtain at deep distance, battlements cut into alternating fang-shapes of uneven height, sections of the parapet walk still bearing iron dragon-standard brackets, the entire length stained with old soot striations.

COLONNADE-OF-CLAWS PROCESSIONAL TERMINUS — Circular dais at the end of a ruined processional colonnade, the central plinth carved as stacked dragon-vertebrae rising three meters, a broken chain of massive iron links still anchored to its crown.
WYRM-SKELETON SUPPORT ARCH — Single massive dragon spine and ribcage repurposed as a load-bearing arch over a gatehouse passage, bones mortared in place and polished smooth by centuries of use.
DRAGON-EYE WINDOW TOWER — Slender stone tower with a single enormous circular window of amber and red glass styled as a slit-pupiled dragon eye, cracked but intact.
CLAW-CARVED BUTTRESS GALLERY — External arcade running the length of a great hall, each buttress terminating in a carved dragon talon gripping the foundation stone, moss-filled joints.

RUNIC DRAGON-GLYPH WALL — Freestanding ceremonial wall thirty feet tall, every surface dense with etched runic dragon-script, base stones displaced outward by root-growth or something pushing from within.
DRAGON-TOOTH BATTLEMENT WALL — Curtain wall capped with alternating crenellations shaped as rows of long curved dragon teeth, wide breach in the northern section melted rather than broken.
HOARD-CRYPT ANTECHAMBER — Low-vaulted entry chamber preceding a sealed vault, floor inlaid with a mosaic wyrm in tarnished gold tile, iron door buckled outward from the far side.
BONE-PILLAR SANCTUM — Circular inner sanctum using stacked and mortared dragon vertebrae as columns, domed ceiling intact, central floor depression filled with fused coins and melted armor.
DRAGON-CULT BELL-ARCH — Massive stone arch standing alone in a ruined courtyard, a great cracked bell suspended from its crown bearing an embossed coiling dragon, rope long rotted.
SCALED-DOME RELIQUARY — Broad low dome with exterior surface carved entirely in overlapping stone scales, interior housing a cracked obsidian plinth displaying a single enormous shed tooth.

DRAGON-TEMPLE FORECOURT — broad terrace of cracked paving stones before a ruined temple, low parapet walls topped with carved dragon-tooth merlons, a headless stone wyrm statue dominating the forecourt center.

CLIFF-CUT DRAGON-FACE CARVING — enormous wyrm-face carved into a cliff escarpment at midground, the mouth forming a functional cave entrance thirty feet wide, the carved eyes deeply shadowed by overhanging brow-stone.

HOARD-VAULT ANTECHAMBER — low-ceilinged vestibule before a sealed vault door, walls inlaid with hammered bronze scale-pattern panels, the floor worn in a broad oval path by generations of circling movement.

DRAGON-CULT GATEHOUSE — massive twin-towered gatehouse with the archway formed by two interlocking carved wyrm-bodies, each tower capped by a dragon-wing silhouette parapet, ironwork gates fused permanently shut by old heat.

RUNIC-GLYPH STANDING WALL — lone freestanding wall remnant of a larger structure, every exposed stone face densely covered in carved runic dragon-glyphs, the topmost courses collapsed leaving the inscription incomplete mid-sentence.
SCALED-DOME SANCTUM — squat domed building at midground, its exterior dome surface carved in overlapping scale-relief, the dome's crown open to sky where the capstone was removed or blasted outward.
DRAGON-RIDER BARRACKS — long low stone building against a canyon wall, wide stable-like bays open along its length instead of doors, iron perch-bars spanning each bay at head height, all empty.

WING-VAULTED SANCTUM — Barrel-vaulted inner chamber where ceiling ribs spread outward like folded dragon wings from a central keystone carved as a coiled wyrm, plaster fallen to reveal raw chisel marks beneath.

RUNIC-GATEWAY — Freestanding stone arch standing alone on a blasted plain, every surface dense with carved dragon-glyphs filled with old pigment, the ground beneath the arch vitrified to smooth black glass.

PETRIFIED-FLAME CHANDELIERS HALL — Long feasting hall with a dozen hanging stone-cast flame chandeliers glowing dull orange without heat source, walls etched floor-to-ceiling with wyrm-lineage genealogies, roof partially collapsed at far end.

DRAGON-EYE TOWER — Cylindrical watchtower with three enormous elliptical dragon-eye window openings spaced at intervals, slit-pupil ironwork intact, tower leaning slightly east, outer face fire-scarred from base to mid-height.

WYRM-SKELETON BRIDGE — Arched crossing built through and around an actual dragon ribcage fused with cut stone, vertebrae integrated into the parapet rail, femur-pillar supports rising from the riverbed below.

CLAW-CARVED BUTTRESS HALL — Broad undercroft with every exterior buttress deeply incised with claw patterns descending from capital to footing, one buttress sheared clean away, its absence opening a long crack in the vault.

DRAGON-TOOTH CRENELLATED RAMPART — Long curtain wall crowning a ridge, every merlon carved to a sharp tooth-point in wyrm-fang profile, the parapet walk littered with cracked scales the size of shields.

DRAGON-CULT CRYPT — Underground charnel space with arched ceiling, niches holding robed skeletal figures seated in reverent posture, central floor-drain crusted black, walls displaying painted wyrm-panels faded to ghost-traces.

SCALED-STONE GATEHOUSE — Twin-towered gateway with outer faces clad in carved stone scales overlapping like true hide, portcullis long fused into raised position by old heat, threshold stones worn concave by enormous repeated passage.

DRAGON-CULT MONASTERY — Severe rectangular complex of blackened ashlar, wing-shaped flying buttresses spanning the nave, every window a dragon-eye lancet of amber glass casting reptilian light across the courtyard.

DRAGON-TOMB MARKER FIELD — Wide moorland cemetery of standing dragon-fang obelisks, each marker etched with runic wyrm-glyphs, some listing severely, surrounded by scorched ground where nothing grows.

DRAGON-FORTIFIED KEEP — Squat curtain-wall fortress with claw-carved buttresses reinforcing every corner tower, the gatehouse lintel bearing a carved wyrm swallowing its own tail, portcullis long torn free.

RUNIC DRAGON-GLYPH CHAMBER — Low barrel-vaulted undercroft visible through a broken floor above, all four walls covered edge-to-edge in carved runic dragon-scripture, a single unlit brazier at the chamber center.

AERIE-FORTRESS — Cliff-edge defensive structure built above a sheer drop, open-roofed central court sized for landing dragons, iron tethering posts still upright, massive staining from rendered dragon-fat torch-fuel.

SCALED-ARCH GATE — Freestanding ceremonial gateway spanning a dry road, the arch interior carved in overlapping scale-courses, keystone shaped as a dragon-skull from which both arch-curves descend to ground.

WING-SHAPED FLYING-BUTTRESS HALL — Massive cathedral flank visible at midground, every flying buttress carved into an outstretched wing form, the stone wings spanning forty feet each, lichen-covered and asymmetrically cracked.

WYRM-SKELETON SUPPORTED VAULT — Underground ceremonial vault ceiling supported entirely by an intact wyrm-skeleton bent into an arch, the ribcage forming the barrel-vault ribs, firelight making shadows crawl across the bones.

RUNIC DRAGON-GLYPH GATEWAY — Freestanding stone gateway arch at midground, every surface covered edge-to-edge in dragon-ward runes, the arch stones slightly displaced as something large passed through them from the other side.

SCALED-ROOF KEEP — Compact keep with its entire roof constructed of overlapping stone scale-tiles in the fashion of dragon hide, the scales individually large as paving stones, darkened and heat-warped at the southwest corner.

DRAGON-CULT SANCTUM — Below-ground circular chamber accessible by wide descending stair, walls lined with carved dragon-worshipper relief carvings, central fire-pit containing cold ash three feet deep, draconic altar bowl cracked clean through.

WING-SHAPED GATEHOUSE — Enormous paired buttresses curving outward and upward like folded wings frame a fortress gate, the stonework fire-blackened, the arch keystone carved into a snarling wyrm-head.
DRAGON-SHRINE GROTTO — A natural cave widened by deliberate carving, its walls incised with overlapping scale patterns, a raised stone dais at centre bearing a cracked draconic idol.
WYRM-SKELETON NAVE — The fossilised spine of a colossal dragon forms the central ridge-beam of a roofless ruin, ribs arching outward as natural vaulting, grass growing through the floor.
SCALED-BUTTRESS CATHEDRAL — Flying buttresses carved to resemble folded dragon necks connect nave wall to outer piers, the stonework pale limestone weathered to soft grey, one buttress fully severed.
DRAGON-CULT OSSUARY — Vaulted underground chapel where dragon teeth and claws are mortared into decorative wall-niches, candle recesses carved between them, the air thick with calcite dust.

CLAW-CARVED FORTIFICATION — A curtain wall whose outer face bears deep diagonal gouges raked by enormous talons, the damaged sections patched with mismatched stone, parapets rebuilt lower than original height.
DRAGON-GLYPH COLONNADE — A ceremonial processional lined with square stone piers, each face covered top-to-bottom in dense runic dragon-glyphs, the far end terminating at a collapsed ceremonial arch.
AERIE TOWER — A tall hexagonal stone spire with no interior floors, open at the summit to a wide stone landing ring, interior walls scratched smooth by generations of roosting claws.

DRACONIC TRIUMPHAL ARCH — A freestanding ceremonial archway of dark granite, its voussoirs carved as interlocking dragon scales, the keystone a roaring wyrm-face, base buried to knee-height in accumulated rubble.

WING-SHAPED FLYING BUTTRESSES — Cathedral exterior buttresses sculpted as extended dragon wings, the membrane stonework pierced with tracery openings, each wingtip curling into a gargoyle head exhaling a frozen stone flame toward the courtyard below.

DRAGON-EYE WINDOW — A circular clerestory window thirty feet across set in a ribbed stone eye-socket frame, the leaded glass in amber and slit-pupil black, projecting a reptilian shadow across the sanctuary floor at midday.

WYRM-SKELETON SUPPORT — A great hall where the full articulated skeleton of an ancient wyrm has been incorporated as a structural element, its skull serving as the entrance arch, ribcage spanning the central bay overhead.

PETRIFIED-FLAME CHANDELIER — A suspended iron armature wound with petrified dragonfire frozen mid-burst, the stone flames translucent amber, catching torchlight below and scattering warm orange fragments across the vaulted hall's carved-scale ceiling.

RUNIC-GLYPH GATEWAY — A freestanding ceremonial arch of dark basalt, every surface covered edge-to-edge in dragon-contract runic script at finger-width depth, the keystone bearing a single unreadable glyph larger than a man's torso, partly defaced.

VAULT-OF-SCROLLS ANNEX — A low domed chamber adjoining the main temple, interior walls lined with sealed stone niches, each niche door bearing a different dragon-breed sigil, the dome ceiling painted with a star-map used for dragon migration charting.

WING-SHAPED FLYING-BUTTRESS CATHEDRAL — A vast stone cathedral whose lateral buttresses are sculpted as swept dragon wings, the stonework cracked along tension lines, rose windows replaced by dragon-eye amber glass.
WYRM-SKELETON SUPPORT HALL — A long feasting hall whose roof is held by preserved wyrm spines mortared upright as columns, the scale-texture still visible beneath centuries of accumulated soot.
PETRIFIED-FLAME CHANDELIER VAULT — A stone-ribbed vault hung with enormous petrified-flame chandeliers cast in iron, each arm shaped as a coiled neck and open mouth, cold and corroded now.

CLAW-CARVED BUTTRESS RUIN — A collapsed transept where surviving buttresses show deep claw gouges running diagonally across their faces, the stone edges still sharp despite evident age and weathering.
RUNIC-GLYPH GATE — A freestanding ceremonial gate of dark limestone, its posts and lintel dense with etched dragon-runes, the arch keystone carved as a small coiled wyrm biting its own tail.
DRAGON-RIDER HALL — A long great-hall with saddle-racks still bolted to stone pillars, rider-insignia carved above each rack, the far wall dominated by a painted-stone mural of formation flight.

SCALED-STONE AMPHITHEATER — An open ritual amphitheater with tiered seating faced in overlapping stone scales, the central performance floor bearing a dragon-glyph mosaic, partially obscured by encroaching turf.

DRAGON-FORTIFIED CURTAIN WALL — A wide curtain wall whose merlons are shaped as alternating dragon heads and raised wings, arrow-loops cut through open wyrm mouths, the entire eastern stretch collapsed into rubble.

WYRM-SKELETON SUPPORTED BRIDGE — Arched stone bridge where the spandrel is braced by an actual dragon ribcage mortared into the masonry, the bones yellowed and mossy, the keystone carved with a crowned wyrm-head relief.

CLAW-CARVED BUTTRESS CHAPEL — Small vaulted chapel where every exterior buttress terminates in a carved dragon claw gripping the foundation plinth, the interior altar bearing a single obsidian egg resting in a cracked stone cradle.

SCALED-TILE COURTYARD — Wide inner courtyard paved in hexagonal basalt tiles carved to resemble overlapping dragon scales, a dry fountain at its center shaped as a rearing wyrm, the surrounding arcade walls heat-blistered and crumbling.

WING-VAULTED THRONE HALL — Grand audience chamber where the ceiling vault is carved to suggest a spread dragon wing in full extension, each stone feather individually detailed, the throne dais below cracked and tilted by a collapsed column.

AERIE-BRIDGE — Narrow stone span connecting two cliff-face platforms at considerable altitude, the parapet walls scored horizontally by talon marks, the midpoint of the bridge sagging where stone was softened by repeated close-range flame.

DRAGON-TEMPLE ANTECHAMBER — Low-ceilinged approach hall of polished black marble, its walls set with rows of petrified dragon eyes in iron mounts, the floor grooved with channels designed to drain ritual dragonblood toward a central glyph-carved collection basin.

CLAW-CARVED BUTTRESS ARCADE — Ruined arcade of six Gothic-proportioned buttresses, each stone face deeply gouged by actual draconic claws in repeated territorial marking, the damage so old that moss has colonized every groove, lending the carvings an eerie organic texture.

VAULT-OF-OATHS — Deep subterranean chamber reached by a switchback stair, its barrel-vaulted ceiling carved with the names of every dragon-rider sworn here, iron torch-brackets shaped as open draconic jaws lining both walls at shoulder height, the air heavy with ancient char.

DRAGON-GLYPH STANDING WALL — Isolated curtain-wall fragment, all that remains of a larger fortification, its interior face covered top to bottom in layered runic dragon-glyphs carved by successive generations of dragon cultists, the oldest inscriptions worn nearly smooth by weather and touch.

DRAGON-TOOTH CRENELLATION PARAPET — Outer wall rampart of a ruined citadel, its entire parapet formed from alternating massive stone merlons shaped as dragon teeth, several broken or missing entirely, the surviving ones stained rust-brown by old dragonblood that seeped from injured beasts landing here.

DRAGON-CULT CHAPTER HOUSE — Low rectangular hall adjoining a collapsed transept, its interior walls lined with stone benches facing a central lectern shaped as a rearing wyrm, shelves of dragon-bone reliquaries visible in the recessed alcoves carved into every wall.

DRAGON-EYE-WINDOW CATHEDRAL — High gothic nave of ash-grey limestone, enormous rose windows cut in the form of slit-pupilled dragon eyes, the coloured glass casting amber and crimson across the pew-stones.

WING-SHAPED FLYING-BUTTRESS NAVE — Elongated hall whose exterior stone buttresses arc and taper like folded dragon wings, the masonry joints sealed with dark mortar rumoured to contain powdered dragon-bone.

WYRM-SKELETON-SUPPORT VAULT — Underground treasury whose ceiling is braced by actual dragon ribcage bones mortared into the stonework, the enormous curved ribs spanning thirty feet between each lateral stone pier.

DRAGON-TOOTH CRENELLATION BATTLEMENT — Long curtain-wall parapet where every merlon is carved into an individual fang shape, the wall-walk beneath stained with rust-red discolouration from iron chain anchors once used for restraint.

RUNIC-GLYPH GATEHOUSE — Heavy twin-towered gate of dark basalt, every dressed stone face incised with interlocking dragon runic bands, the runes inlaid with dull bronze that catches firelight in the deep grooves.

CLAW-CARVED BUTTRESS CHANCEL — Apsed sanctuary of pale limestone, the exterior buttresses cut into claw-forms at their bases, each stone talon gripping the foundation course, the apse window a half-lidded dragon eye.

DRAGON-CULT SCRIPTORIUM TOWER — Slender five-storey tower of mortared fieldstone, its narrow windows framed by carved wyrm-serpent borders, the ground floor sealed by iron doors bearing a branded dragon-circle sigil.

SCALED-ARCH BRIDGE APPROACH — Wide stone bridge leading to a ruined keep, the arch soffit carved in scale relief matching dragon-belly patterning, the keystone face a roaring wyrm-head worn soft by weather.

HOARD-GATE VAULT ENTRANCE — Broad low arch of heat-blackened granite leading into a deep-cut hillside chamber, the door-frame stones fused at the corners by ancient dragonfire, the threshold stones bowed by immense settled weight.

DRAGON-EYE WINDOW HALL — Long great-hall at midground, its upper clerestory pierced by oval windows of amber glass arranged to suggest a lidded reptilian eye; one window is shattered inward, amber shards on the floor below.

DRAGON-CULT-MONASTERY GATE — Barbican of dark granite, twin towers connected by a span carved with kneeling figures offering flame to a great wyrm above the arch; one tower has been bitten through near its base.

RUNIC-GLYPH FORTIFICATION WALL — Curtain wall of black ashlar stone at deep distance, every third block incised with dragon-rune wards; entire sections of the wall have been pushed inward and lie as rubble, wards incomplete mid-sentence.

DRAGON-TOOTH CRENELLATION RAMPART — Long curtain rampart at deep distance, its walkway edged with alternating triangular merlons shaped as bared dragon teeth; scorch lines run vertically from each gap, still darker than the surrounding stone.

VAULT-OF-ANCIENT-OATHS HALL — Barrel-vaulted chamber of pale limestone, its walls lined with carved dragon-heads at head height; each carved mouth holds a rusted iron bracket once used to display treaty scrolls, all brackets now empty and bent.
WYRM-TOMB — Mountain-cut burial chamber entrance, the doorframe carved as an open dragon maw, upper jaw forming the lintel, lower jaw the threshold step, teeth intact and sharp.
